subject: general
question: In which of the following states of India is the maximum extent of alluvial soil found?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttar Pradesh**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Uttar Pradesh** has the maximum extent of alluvial soil in India.
 
• Alluvial soils are widespread in the northern plains and the river valleys of India.
 
• These soils are formed by the deposition of sediments brought down by rivers.
 
• Uttar Pradesh, being part of the Indo-Gangetic plain, is predominantly covered with alluvial soil.
 
• This type of soil is highly fertile and suitable for agriculture, supporting the cultivation of crops like wheat, rice, sugarcane, and pulses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Alluvial soils are classified into two types: Bhangar (old alluvial soil) and Khadar (new alluvial soil).
 
• Bhangar soils are found on higher lands and are less fertile, while Khadar soils are found in the floodplains and are more fertile.
 
• The Indo-Gangetic plain, covering states like Punjab, Haryana, Bihar, and West Bengal, is also rich in alluvial soil.
 
• Alluvial soil is characterized by its light texture, good porosity, and high water retention capacity, making it ideal for intensive agriculture.
